Main.sentence: The two-state solution is a proposed approach to resolving the ___E:Israeli–Palestinian conflict U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli%E2%80%93Palestinian_conflict)___ , by creating two states on the territory of the former ___E:Mandatory Palestine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandatory_Palestine)___ .

It is often contrasted with the ___E:one-state solution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-state_solution)___ , which is the establishment a single state in former Mandatory Palestine with equal rights for all its inhabitants.
The two-state solution is supported by many countries and the ___E:Palestinian Authority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_Authority)___ .
Israel currently does not support the idea, though it has in the past.

The first proposal for separate Jewish and Arab states in the territory was made by the British ___E:Peel Commission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peel_Commission)___ report in 1937.  In 1947, the ___E:United Nations General Assembly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_General_Assembly)___ adopted a ___E:partition plan for Palestine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Partition_Plan_for_Palestine)___ , leading to the ___E:1948 Palestine war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Palestine_war)___ .

As a result, ___E:Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel)___ was established on the area the UN had proposed for the Jewish state, as well as almost 60% of the area proposed for the Arab state.

Israel took control of ___E:West Jerusalem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Jerusalem)___ , which was meant to be part of an international zone. Jordan took control of ___E:East Jerusalem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Jerusalem)___ and what became known as the ___E:West Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bank)___ , ___E:annexing it the following year U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordanian_annexation_of_the_West_Bank)___ .

The territory which became the ___E:Gaza Strip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip)___ was ___E:occupied by Egypt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occupation_of_the_Gaza_Strip_by_Egypt)___ but never annexed.

Since the 1967 ___E:Six-Day War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-Day_War)___ , both the West Bank (including East Jerusalem) and Gaza Strip have been militarily occupied by Israel, becoming known as the ___E:Palestinian territories U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_territories)___ .

The ___E:Palestine Liberation Organization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestine_Liberation_Organization)___ has accepted the concept of a two-state solution since the 1982 Arab Summit, on the basis of an independent Palestinian state based in the West Bank, Gaza and East Jerusalem.

In 2017, ___E:Hamas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamas)___ announced their ___E:revised charter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Hamas_charter)___ , which claims to accept the idea of a Palestinian state within the 1967 borders, but without recognising the statehood of Israel.  ___E:Diplomatic efforts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli%E2%80%93Palestinian_peace_process)___ have centred around realizing a two-state solution, starting from the failed ___E:2000 Camp David Summit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Camp_David_Summit)___ and ___E:the Clinton Parameters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Clinton_Parameters)___ , followed by the ___E:Taba Summit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taba_Summit)___ in 2001. The failure of the Camp David summit to reach an agreed two-state solution formed the backdrop to the commencement of the ___E:Second Intifada U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Intifada)___ , the violent consequences of which marked a turning point among both peoples’ attitudes.

A two-state solution also formed the basis of the ___E:Arab Peace Initiative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_Peace_Initiative)___ , the ___E:2006–2008 peace offer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Realignment_plan)___ , and the ___E:2013–14 peace talks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Israeli%E2%80%93Palestinian_peace_talks)___ .
Currently there is no two-state solution proposal being negotiated between Israel and Palestinians.

The ___E:Palestinian Authority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_Authority)___ supports the idea of a two-state solution;  Israel at times has also supported the idea, but currently rejects the creation of a Palestinian state.

Long-serving Israeli prime minister ___E:Benjamin Netanyahu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu)___ stated his objection to a Palestinian state on two occasions, in 2015 and 2023.    Former Israeli prime ministers ___E:Ehud Barak U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ehud_Barak)___ and ___E:Ehud Olmert U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ehud_Olmert)___ in late 2023 expressed support for a two-state solution.

Public support among Israelis and Palestinians (measured separately) for "the concept of the two-state solution" have varied between above and below 50%, partially depending on how the question was phrased.

The major points of contention include the specific boundaries of the two states (though most proposals are based on the ___E:1967 lines U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Line_(Israel))___ ), the ___E:status of Jerusalem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Status_of_Jerusalem)___ , the ___E:Israeli settlements U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_settlements)___ and the ___E:right of return of Palestinian refugees U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_right_of_return)___ .

Observers have described the current situation in the whole territory, with the ___E:Israeli occupation of the West Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_occupation_of_the_West_Bank)___ and ___E:blockade of the Gaza Strip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockade_of_the_Gaza_Strip)___ , as one of de facto Israeli sovereignty.
The two-state solution is an alternative to the one-state solution and what observers consider a de facto one-state reality.

Following the ___E:October 7 attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_7_attacks)___ and the subsequent ___E:Gaza war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war)___ , multiple governments restarted discussions on a two-state solution.
This received pushback from Israel's government, especially from prime minister Netanyahu.

On 26 September 2024, Saudi Foreign Minister Prince ___E:Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faisal_bin_Farhan_Al_Saud)___ and Norway's Foreign Minister ___E:Espen Barth Eide U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Espen_Barth_Eide)___ co-chaired a meeting of representatives of about 90 countries, held on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, to launch a global alliance for a two-state solution.

In the wake of ___E:Jewish migration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aliyah)___ from Europe in the context of ___E:Zionism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zionism)___ and ___E:intercommunal conflict U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercommunal_conflict_in_Mandatory_Palestine)___ in ___E:Mandatory Palestine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandatory_Palestine)___ , the first proposal for the creation of Jewish and Arab states in the ___E:British Mandate of Palestine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandatory_Palestine)___ was made by the British ___E:Peel Commission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peel_Commission)___ report of 1937 led by ___E:William Peel, 1st Earl Peel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Peel,_1st_Earl_Peel)___ .

The plan maintained a mandate covering a small area containing ___E:Jerusalem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerusalem)___ and allotted the poorest lands of Palestine, including the ___E:Negev Desert U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Negev_Desert)___ , and areas that are known today as the ___E:West Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bank)___ and the ___E:Gaza Strip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip)___ to the Arabs; while most of the coastline and some of Palestine's most fertile agricultural land in the ___E:Galilee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galilee)___ were allotted to the Jews.  Consequently, the recommended partition proposal was rejected by the Arab community of Palestine, and was accepted by most of the Jewish leadership.
Partition was again proposed by the ___E:1947 UN Partition Plan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1947_UN_Partition_Plan)___ for the division of Palestine.
It proposed a three-way division, again with Jerusalem held separately, under international control.

The partition plan was accepted by ___E:Jewish Agency for Palestine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_Agency_for_Palestine)___ and most Zionist factions who viewed it as a stepping stone to territorial expansion at an opportune time.   The ___E:Arab Higher Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_Higher_Committee)___ , the ___E:Arab League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_League)___ and other Arab leaders and governments rejected it on the basis that Arabs formed a two-thirds majority and owned a majority of the lands.

They also indicated an unwillingness to accept any form of territorial division,  arguing that it violated the principles of ___E:national self-determination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-determination)___ in the ___E:UN Charter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Charter)___ .
They announced their intention to take all necessary measures to prevent the implementation of the resolution.

Subsequently, the ___E:Intercommunal conflict U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercommunal_conflict_in_Mandatory_Palestine)___ in Palestine gave way to ___E:civil war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1947%E2%80%931948_civil_war_in_Mandatory_Palestine)___  and the plan was not implemented.

At the end of the British Mandate, with the ___E:establishment of the State of Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Establishment_of_the_State_of_Israel)___ and entry of Arab regular armies into what had been Mandatory Palestine, the ___E:1948 war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Palestine_war)___ became an ___E:international conflict U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Arab%E2%80%93Israeli_War)___ .

At the end of the war, the ___E:Green Line U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Line_(Israel))___ established by the ___E:1949 Armistice Agreements U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1949_Armistice_Agreements)___ became the de facto borders of the State of Israel.

The war resulted in the ___E:fleeing or expulsion of 711,000 Palestinians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Palestinian_exodus)___ , which the Palestinians call Nakba , from the territories which became the state of Israel.

After the ___E:1967 Arab–Israeli war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-Day_War)___ , the United Nations Security Council unanimously passed ___E:resolution 242 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_242)___ calling for Israeli withdrawal from the ___E:territories occupied U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli-occupied_territories)___ during the war, in exchange for "termination of all claims or states of belligerency" and "acknowledgement of sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of every state in the area".

The ___E:Palestine Liberation Organization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestine_Liberation_Organization)___ (PLO), which had been formed in 1964, strongly criticized the resolution, saying that it reduced the question of Palestine to a refugee problem.  : 18
In September 1974, 56 member states proposed that "the question of Palestine" be included as an item in the General Assembly's agenda.

In a resolution adopted on 22 November 1974, the General Assembly affirmed Palestinian rights, which included the "right to self-determination without external interference", "the right to national independence and sovereignty", and the "right to return to their homes and property".
These rights have been affirmed every year since.  : 24

The first indication that the PLO would be willing to accept a two-state solution, on at least an interim basis, was articulated by ___E:Said Hammami U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Said_Hammami)___ in the mid-1970s.

The Israeli ___E:Likud U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Likud)___ party, in its manifesto for the ___E:1977 elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1977_Israeli_legislative_election)___ which it won in a landslide, declared: "Between the sea and the Jordan there will only be Israeli sovereignty."    Similar statements have been made by Israeli Prime Minister ___E:Benjamin Netanyahu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu)___ as late as 18 January 2024.
On 18 July 2024, the Israeli parliament passed a resolution that rejected the establishment of a Palestinian state.

The resolution passed in the Knesset with 68 votes in favour and nine against it. Netanyahu’s coalition with far-right parties co-sponsored the resolution, while the opposition left the session to avoid supporting the statement.

The ___E:Palestinian Declaration of Independence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_Declaration_of_Independence)___ of 15 November 1988, which referenced the ___E:UN Partition Plan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN_Partition_Plan)___ of 1947 and "UN resolutions since 1947" in general, was interpreted as an indirect recognition of the ___E:State of Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_Israel)___ , and support for a two-state solution.
The Partition Plan was invoked to provide legitimacy to Palestinian statehood.
Subsequent clarifications were taken to amount to the first explicit Palestinian recognition of Israel.
The ___E:2017 Hamas charter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Hamas_charter)___ presented the Palestinian state being based on the 1967 borders.

The text says "Hamas considers the establishment of a Palestinian state, sovereign and complete, on the basis of the June 4, 1967, with Jerusalem as its capital and the provision for all the refugees to return to their homeland."  This is in contrast to Hamas' 1988 charter, which previously called for a Palestinian state on all of ___E:Mandatory Palestine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandatory_Palestine)___ .
Nevertheless, even in the 2017 charter, Hamas did not recognize Israel.
In December 2022, ___E:Benjamin Netanyahu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu)___ returned as Prime Minister of Israel, forming the most right-wing government in Israel's history.
Netanyahu's coalition partners rejected the two-state solution.

In February 2023, Netanyahu said he would be willing to grant Palestinians autonomy but not sovereignty, and in any future deal Israel would maintain full security control of the West Bank.  In June 2023, Netanyahu told members of the Knesset that Israel must block the creation of a Palestinian state.

Later in 2023, despite Israeli PM Netanyahu's statement denying the creation of a Palestinian state as a condition for a normalization with Saudi Arabia,    Saudi Arabian crown prince ___E:Mohammed bin Salman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammed_bin_Salman)___ said normalization with Israel was "for the first time real".

This was an apparent reversal of Saudi policy, articulated in the ___E:2002 Arab Peace Initiative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Arab_Peace_Initiative)___ , when Saudi Arabia had offered Israel normalization with the whole Arab world if Israel allows the creation of a Palestinian state.
Israeli  and other officials involved in the negotiations confirmed that the Saudis were considering normalization with Israel without the creation of a Palestinian state.
Many Palestinians worried that Israeli-Saudi normalization would cost them their last significant leverage for Palestinian statehood.
In October 2023, ___E:Hamas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamas)___ launched an attack on Israel.

Numerous sources identified the lack of a Palestinian state as a cause of the war.      The ___E:Associated Press U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press)___ wrote that Palestinians are "in despair over a never-ending occupation in the West Bank and suffocating blockade of Gaza".
After ___E:Netanyahu invaded Gaza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_invasion_of_the_Gaza_Strip)___ , he once again reiterated his opposition to the existence of a Palestinian state.

Security Council resolutions dating back to June 1976 supporting the two-state solution based on the pre-1967 lines were vetoed by the United States,  which supports a two-state solution but argued that the borders must be negotiated directly by the parties.

After the ___E:First Intifada U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Intifada)___ began in 1987, considerable diplomatic work went into negotiations between the parties, beginning with the Madrid Conference in 1991. The most significant of these negotiations was the Oslo Accords, which officially divided Palestinian land into three administrative divisions and created the framework for how much of Israel's political borders with the Palestinian territories function today.

The Accords culminated in the ___E:Camp David 2000 Summit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_David_2000_Summit)___ , and follow-up negotiations at Taba in January 2001, which built explicitly on a two-state framework, but no final agreement was ever reached.

The violent outbreak of the ___E:Second Intifada U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Intifada)___ in 2000 had demonstrated the Palestinian public's disillusionment with the Oslo Accords and convinced many Israelis that the negotiations were in vain.

In 2002, Crown Prince ___E:Abdullah of Saudi Arabia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdullah_of_Saudi_Arabia)___ (who would go on to be King from 2005 to 2015) proposed the Arab Peace Initiative, which garnered the unanimous support of the ___E:Arab League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_League)___ while Israeli leaders continually refuse to discuss the initiative.

President Bush announced his support for a Palestinian state, opening the way for ___E:United Nations Security Council Resolution 1397 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_1397)___ , supporting a two-state solution.  [page needed]

At the ___E:Annapolis Conference U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapolis_Conference)___ in November 2007, three major parties – The PLO, Israel, and the US – agreed on a two-state solution as the outline for negotiations.
However, the summit failed to achieve an agreement. [citation needed]

Following ___E:the conflict U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatah%E2%80%93Hamas_conflict)___ that erupted between the two main Palestinian parties, ___E:Fatah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatah)___ and ___E:Hamas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamas)___ , Hamas ___E:took control U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Gaza_(2007))___ of the Gaza Strip, splintering the Palestinian Authority into two polities, each claiming to be the true representatives of the Palestinian people.

Fatah controlled the ___E:Palestinian National Authority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_National_Authority)___ in the ___E:West Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bank)___ and Hamas ___E:Governed in Gaza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governance_of_the_Gaza_Strip)___ .

The latest initiatives were the ___E:2013–14 Israeli–Palestinian peace talks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Israeli%E2%80%93Palestinian_peace_talks)___ under the guidance of ___E:John Kerry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kerry)___ , the United States Secretary of State.
These talks also failed to reach an agreement.

By 2010, when direct talks were scheduled to be restarted, continued growth of settlements on the West Bank and continued strong support of settlements by the Israeli government had greatly reduced the land and resources that would be available to a Palestinian state, creating doubt among Palestinians and left-wing Israelis that a two-state solution continued to be viable.

In January 2012 the European Union Heads of Mission report on East Jerusalem found that Israel's continuing settlement activities and the fragile situation of the Palestinian population in East Jerusalem, as well in area C, was making a two-state solution less likely.
The Israeli Foreign Ministry rejected this EU report, claiming it was "based on a partial, biased and one sided depiction of realities on the ground".
In May 2012, the EU council stressed its "deep concern about developments on the ground which threaten to make a two-state solution impossible".

On 29 November 2012, the ___E:UN General Assembly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN_General_Assembly)___ voted by 138 to 9, with 46 abstentions, to recognize Palestine as a "non-member observer state".

On the following day, Israeli PM ___E:Benjamin Netanyahu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu)___ announced the building of 3,000 new homes on land to the east of East Jerusalem, in an area referred to as "E-1".

The move was immediately criticized by several countries, including the United States, with Israeli ambassadors being personally called for meetings with government representatives in the United Kingdom, France and Germany, among others.

Israel's decision to build the homes was described by the ___E:Obama administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obama_administration)___ as "counterproductive", while Australia said that the building plans "threaten the viability of a two-state solution".

This is because they claim the proposed E-1 settlement would physically split the lands under the control of the Palestinian National Authority in two, as the extent of the PNA's authority does not extend all the way to the ___E:River Jordan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River_Jordan)___ and the ___E:Dead Sea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_Sea)___ .
Israel's Labor party has voiced support for the two-state solution, with ___E:Isaac Herzog U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Herzog)___ stating it would be "in Israel's interests".

In March 2015, Netanyahu declared that a Palestinian state would not be established during his administration,  while he also stated that he disapproved of the ___E:one-state solution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-state_solution)___ for the ___E:ongoing conflict U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli%E2%80%93Palestinian_conflict)___ between two people.

After the ___E:Trump administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_presidency_of_Donald_Trump)___ 's controversial ___E:decision to recognize Jerusalem as Israel's capital U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_recognition_of_Jerusalem_as_capital_of_Israel)___ in December 2017, Palestinian officials said the policy change "destroys the peace process" and the decision indirectly meant the United States was "abdicating its role as a peace mediator"  because the United States had become a party to the dispute instead of neutral intercessor for negotiations.

A 2021 survey among 521 scholars who have dedicated their professional lives to the study of this region and its politics found that 52 percent of respondents believed the two-state solution is no longer possible.

If a two-state solution is not achieved, 77 percent predict "a ___E:one-state reality U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-state_reality)___ akin to apartheid" and 17 percent "one-state reality with increasing inequality, but not akin to apartheid"; one percent think a ___E:binational state U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binational_state)___ with equal rights for all inhabitants is likely.

UN resolutions affirm the illegality of ___E:settlements in West Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_settlement)___ , including ___E:East Jerusalem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Jerusalem)___ , including ___E:United Nations Security Council Resolution 2334 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_2334)___ passed in December 2016.  As of November 2023, there are at least 700,000 Israeli settlers in the Occupied West Bank and East Jerusalem across 150 settlements and 128 outposts.
More than three-quarters of the existing settlements have been constructed since the ___E:Oslo Accords U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oslo_Accords)___ .

The establishment and expansion of the illegal settlements in the Occupied West Bank constitute a major challenge to the possibility of a two-state solution by "violating Palestinian sovereignty, threatening civil peace and security, jeopardizing water resources, and blocking agricultural development."  This has progressively reduced ___E:Area A and B U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_enclaves)___ of the West Bank territory to a "shrinking archipelago of enclaves".

Proposals have been offered for over 50 post-evacuation compensation of settlers for abandoned property [clarification needed] , as occurred following Israel's ___E:withdrawal of settlements from Gaza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel%27s_unilateral_disengagement_plan#Compensation_and_resettlement)___ in 2005 and from the ___E:Sinai Peninsula U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinai_Peninsula)___ in 1982.  Some settlers in those previous withdrawals were forcibly removed by the IDF.

In a 2002 poll conducted by ___E:PIPA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Program_on_International_Policy_Attitudes)___ , 72% of both Palestinians and Israelis supported at that time a peace settlement based on the 1967 borders so long as each group could be reassured that the other side would be cooperative in making the necessary concessions for such a settlement.

A 2013 Gallup poll found 70% of Palestinians in the West Bank and 48% of Palestinians in Gaza Strip, together with 52% of Israelis supporting "an independent Palestinian state together with the state of Israel".
Support for a two-state solution varies according to the way the question is phrased.
Some Israeli journalists suggest that the Palestinians are unprepared to accept a Jewish State on any terms.

According to one poll, "fewer than 2 in 10 Arabs, both Palestinian and all others, believe in Israel's right to exist as a nation with a Jewish majority."  Another poll, however, cited by the ___E:US State Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_State_Department)___ , suggests that "78 percent of Palestinians and 74 percent of Israelis believe a peace agreement that leads to both states living side by side as good neighbors" is "essential or desirable".

In 2021, a poll by the ___E:Palestinian Center for Policy and Survey Research U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_Center_for_Policy_and_Survey_Research)___ revealed that 39% of Palestinians supported "the concept of the two-state solution", while 59% said they rejected it.  Support is even lower among younger Palestinians; in 2008, then- ___E:U.S. Secretary of State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Secretary_of_State)___ ___E:Condoleezza Rice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condoleezza_Rice)___ noted: "Increasingly, the Palestinians who talk about a two-state solution are my age."  A survey taken before the ___E:outbreak of fighting in 2014 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Protective_Edge)___ by the ___E:Washington Institute for Near East Policy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Institute_for_Near_East_Policy)___ (WINEP) found that 60 percent of Palestinians say the goal of their national movement should be "to work toward reclaiming all of historic Palestine from the river to the sea" compared to just 27 percent who endorse the idea that they should work "to end the occupation of the West Bank and Gaza and achieve a two-state solution." WINEP says that "this is a new finding compared to similar (but not identical) questions asked in the past, when support for a two-state solution typically ranged between 40–55 percent".
By 2020, 40% in Gaza and 26% in the West Bank believe that a negotiated two-state solution should solve the conflict.

Another report, published also in 2021 by the ___E:RAND Corporation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RAND_Corporation)___ , found that also 60% of Israelis across the political spectrum were opposed to a two-state solution.

The two-state solution enjoyed majority support in Israeli polls although there has been some erosion to its prospects over time.  A 2014 Haaretz poll asking "Consider that in the framework of an agreement, most settlers are annexed to Israel, Jerusalem will be divided, refugees won't return to Israel and there will be a strict security arrangement, would you support this agreement?", only 35% of Israelis said yes.

According to a 2021 ___E:PCPSR U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_Center_for_Policy_and_Survey_Research)___ poll, support for a two-state solution among Palestinians and Israeli Jews, as of 2021, had declined to 43 percent and 42 percent, respectively.
According to Middle East experts David Pollock and Catherine Cleveland, as of 2021, the majority of Palestinians said they wanted to reclaim all of historic Palestine, including pre-1967 Israel.
A one-state solution with equal rights for Arabs and Jews was ranked second.

Some researchers argue that the two-state solution has already been implemented because ___E:Jordan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan)___ , which makes up 78% of the former Mandatory Palestine, was originally created as a state for the Arabs.

In December 2022, support for a two-state solution was 33% among Palestinians, 34% among Israeli Jews, and 60% among ___E:Israeli Arabs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_citizens_of_Israel)___ . 82% of Israeli Jews and 75% of Palestinians believed that the other side would never accept the existence of their independent state.

At the end of October 2023, the two-state solution had the support of 71.9% of Israeli Arabs and 28.6% of Israeli Jews.  Prior to the ___E:October 7 attack U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_7_attack)___ , according to ___E:Gallup U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallup,_Inc.)___ , just 24% of Palestinians supported a two-state solution, a drop from 59% in 2012.

___E:Ehud Olmert U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ehud_Olmert)___ , Israel's Prime Minister from 2006 to 2009, told Politico on 16 October 2023 that the two-state solution "is the only real political solution for this lifelong conflict".
On 6 November 2023, he told ___E:CBC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBC_News)___ that "a two-state solution should still be the goal of the Israeli government".

___E:Ehud Barak U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ehud_Barak)___ , Israel's Prime Minister from 1999 to 2001 and Minister of Defense from 2007 to 2013, told ___E:TIME U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_(magazine))___ on 6 November 2023 that "The right way is to look to the two-state solution".

Interviewed by ___E:Ezra Klein U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ezra_Klein)___ on 8 December 2023, Nimrod Novik, a member of the executive committee of ___E:Commanders for Israel's Security U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commanders_for_Israel%27s_Security)___ (CIS), reiterated the CIS's view that the two-state solution is "the only solution that [...] serves Israel's security and well-being long-term."

In the 1950s and 1960s, King Hussein of Jordan and his officials promoted the idea that "Jordan is Palestine and Palestine is Jordan," aiming to present Jordanians and Palestinians as one unified people with a shared destiny.

Following the 1967 Six-Day War, which resulted in Jordan losing the West Bank to Israel, Israeli leaders ___E:Yigal Allon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yigal_Allon)___ and ___E:Abba Eban U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abba_Eban)___ presented King Hussein with the ___E:Allon Plan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allon_Plan)___ , which suggested returning parts of the West Bank to Jordan.

In 1988, King Hussein renounced Jordan's claims to the West Bank and Palestinian affairs.

Despite Jordanian opposition to the confederation idea, leading to limited advocacy from Israeli leaders,  renewed interest in the Jordanian option has emerged as a potential solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
